problem:
Which of the following sets are orthogonal?

- $U={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}$
- $V={[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 0 \\ -6\end{aligned}]}$
- $W={[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -10\end{aligned}]}$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following sets are orthogonal?

- $U={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$
- $V={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$
- $W={[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of the given sets as 
${{u}_{1},{u}_{2},{u}_{3}},$ 
${{v}_{1},{v}_{2}},$ and 
${{w}_{1},{w}_{2}},$ respectively. 

The sets $U,V,$ and $W$ are orthogonal if the following conditions on each set hold:

- ${u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2}=0,\,{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{3}=0,\,{u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{3}=0.$

- ${v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2}=0.$

- ${w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2}=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our sets in turn.

- For the set $U,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=-1+3-1-1=0 & ✓ \\ {u}_{1}\cdot {u}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=1+0-2+1=0 & ✓ \\ {u}_{2}\cdot {u}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=-1+0+2-1=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $U$ is orthogonal.

- For the set $V,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=2-1-1=0 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set $V$ is orthogonal.

- For the set $W,$ notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{w}_{1}\cdot {w}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -8\end{aligned}]=-15+24=9\ne 0 & \times \end{aligned}
$$

So, $W$ is not an orthogonal set.

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "$U$ and $V$ only".
